newsitem.title: USA: Calif. delays vote on Edison San Onofre plan.
newsitem.headline: Calif. delays vote on Edison San Onofre plan.

text.p: California's Coastal Commission decided late Tuesday to delay a vote on what steps Southern California Edison Co must take to address environmental concerns linked to its San Onofre nuclear power plant.
The commission said it will next meet in mid-November, when public comment will resume and a final vote may be taken.

SoCal Edison, a unit of Edison International, is seeking to revise a 1991 agreement to construct a 300-acre artificial kelp reef off the coast of San Clemente, Calif., which it says it not justified by scientific evidence.

The company is instead offering to build a smaller, 17-acre reef in addition to projects, like fish hatcheries, it has already undertaken to make up for the environmental impact of the ocean water intake at its San Onofre nuclear plant.
The staff of the state Coastal Commission has proposed a compromise plan for a 122-acre reef to be funded by proceeds from a $19.27 million trust fund paid for by Edison.
Edison owns 75 percent of the San Onofre project, which consists of one 1,070 megawatt (MW) unit and one 1,080 MW unit.
Enova Corp's San Diego Gas and Electric Co holds a 20 percent stake in the plant and two municipal utilities share the remaining five percent.
